messages:
monitor-bot: ALERT: node-gpu-142 (us-west-2) nvme_iops_spike detected. p99 nvme latency 3.2s, iowait 45%, affected pods: gpu-infer-*, eviction starts.

ashley: seeing kernel logs for node-gpu-142: 'nvme nvme0: I/O 3877 queued' and repeated CRC/media warnings. Not just latency — SMART shows increasing media errors.

mohit: ran quick fio on node-gpu-142 in maintenance window: random write 4k rwmix=10 saturates at ~220k iops then huge latency spikes. Disk util hits 99%.

lena: could be a write-heavy checkpoint pattern + ephemeral volume not being trimmed. Do we have any recent changes to checkpoint frequency?

ashley: think a large batch rollout yesterday created lots of small syncs. Also noticed ephemeral-cleanup cron failed on several nodes for last 12h.

ops-oncall: cordoning node-gpu-142 and starting drain now. moving 4 high-priority pods -> other pool.

ashley: mitigation idea: temporarily throttle write I/O for gpu jobs via cgroups io.max on /dev/nvme0n1, plus add fstrim at teardown.

mohit: agree. quick kernel-level throttle:
```
# example for cgroupt v2 (echo values under /sys/fs/cgroup/io)
echo "8:0 1048576" > /sys/fs/cgroup/gpu-jobs/io.max  # 1MB/s cap per cgroup (tune)
```

lena: also add a systemd tmpfiles cleanup and fstrim service on ephemeral teardown to reduce wear and free blocks. something like:
```
[Unit]
Description=Trim ephemeral on shutdown
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/sbin/fstrim -av || true
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

mohit: ran smartctl -a on node-gpu-142:
```
=== START OF INFORMATION SECTION ===
Device Model: NVMeFlashX 3.2TB
SMART overall-health self-assessment test: FAILED
Media and Data Integrity Errors: 1245
```
This looks like real wear, not just transient.

ashley: logged vendor RMA for that host, marking as degraded. Schedule replacement after draining.

ops-oncall: for short-term, I modified autoscaler to spin up 3 extra dedicated GPU hosts in us-west-2 to absorb load. Note: cost hit estimated +$1.8k/day while we rebalance.

lena: we should also throttle application-level checkpoint bursts: buffer to tmpfs and async flush with rate limiting. Add to best-practices doc for model training/inference.

mohit: creating a small playbook for oncall with commands: `fio`, `smartctl -a`, `nvme error-log`, `nvme fw-log`, how to apply `io.max`, and drain steps. Will post PR to infra runbooks.

sre-bot: Incident INF-2341 created (severity: medium) — owners: @ashley, @mohit.

ashley: immediate action list: 1) drain/rebuild 1 node (done for 142), 2) land io.max throttle for gpu job cgroups (in progress), 3) enable ephemeral fstrim service (PR), 4) vendor RMA, 5) postmortem after stabilization.

mohit: note on metrics — add nvme media error counter and write amplification dashboard to prod grafana. current alerts only watch latency, not SMART.

ops-oncall: rolling drain finished for two more nodes, traffic stable but token throughput for hosted inference dipped ~12% during reshuffle.

lena: good catch. also check whether ephemeral image builder left large checkpoint blobs on /tmp between jobs. will audit builders.

ashley: I'll draft a short ops postmortem and circulation plan. everyone add any missing mitigation steps to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:

mohit: PR for ephemeral-cleanup systemd + patch to runner that does fstrim on teardown is up for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/487

ashley: thanks. once PR merges we can flip the autoscaler down and avoid more on-demand capacity.

sre-bot: Incident INF-2341 status updated to 'mitigated' at 1768954599.
